name: Education Prompts
intro: Templates for lesson design, rubrics, and differentiation. The teacher remains the judge of accuracy and fit; never paste student names or records into a prompt.

templates.tip: Anchoring to the specific standard keeps the plan gradeable against what the class actually must cover.
templates.title: Lesson plan builder
templates.prompt: Build a lesson plan. Subject: {SUBJECT}, grade {GRADE}, duration {MINUTES}, standard or objective, verbatim: {STANDARD}. Structure: measurable objective in student-visible language, do-now starter (5 minutes), direct instruction outline with the two most common misconceptions and how to surface them, guided practice activity, independent practice, exit ticket with three questions mapped to the objective, and materials list. Include one modification for students above level and one for students needing support.

templates.tip: Observable-behavior language (cites two sources) grades faster and argues less than quality adjectives (good use of sources).
templates.title: Rubric generator
templates.prompt: Create a rubric for this assignment: {ASSIGNMENT_DESCRIPTION}. Grade level: {GRADE}. Criteria to assess: {LIST, e.g. thesis, evidence, organization, conventions}. Four performance levels: Exceeds, Meets, Approaching, Beginning. Every cell must describe observable work products (counts, presence, accuracy), not quality adjectives. Weight the criteria and show points per cell summing to {TOTAL} points. Add a three-line student-facing summary of what Meets looks like.

templates.tip: Same concept at three depths is the fastest reusable artifact in a mixed-readiness classroom.
templates.title: Differentiated explanations
templates.models: Any; verify subject accuracy at each level.
templates.prompt: Explain {CONCEPT} three times for a grade {GRADE} class: 1) foundation version, concrete example first, no vocabulary beyond grade level, 80 words; 2) on-level version with the correct academic vocabulary introduced and defined, 120 words; 3) extension version connecting the concept to {ADJACENT_TOPIC} with one challenge question, 120 words. Then give one visual or physical demonstration usable with the whole class, and two check-for-understanding questions per level.
